about: Thinking Machines Lab is a San Francisco AI research and product company founded in 2025 by former OpenAI CTO Mira Murati, with co-founders including John Schulman. It focuses on collaborative AI systems and released Tinker, a fine-tuning product. It raised $2bn in seed funding in 2025 at a $12bn valuation led by Andreessen Horowitz, with Nvidia and AMD, and has been reported as raising more at a much higher valuation. Private. Heavily covered in tech media; no consumer products yet.

wiki.title: Thinking Machines Lab
wiki.text: Thinking Machines Lab Inc. is an American artificial intelligence (AI) startup founded by Mira Murati, the former chief technology officer of OpenAI. Their flagship model is Inkling, an open weights large language model.

about: Dayforce (formerly Ceridian) is a Minneapolis-based cloud human capital management software company, supplying payroll, HR, time and attendance, benefits and talent tools to mid-market and large employers in North America and abroad. Revenue is above $1.8bn. Thoma Bravo agreed to take it private in 2025 in an $12.3bn deal, after which it left the NYSE (DAY). B2B software with solid HR industry recognition, and little consumer awareness.

about: Clio is a Burnaby, British Columbia cloud legal practice management software company, serving law firms with case management, billing, client intake and AI tools (Clio Manage, Clio Grow, Clio Work), with over 150,000 users. It raised $900m in 2025 at a $5bn valuation and agreed to buy vLex for about $1bn. Founded in 2008. Private. B2B software with strong awareness among lawyers and little in the general public.

wiki.title: Clio
wiki.what: Muse of history in Ancient Greek mythology
wiki.text: In Greek mythology, Clio, also spelled Kleio, Cleio, or Cleo, is the muse of history, or in a few mythological accounts, the muse of lyre-playing.

about: Quantum Computing Inc. is a Hoboken, New Jersey company, listed on Nasdaq (QUBT), developing photonic quantum technologies such as thin-film lithium niobate chips and quantum optics for sensing, computing and security. It has raised capital through private placements, giving it a cash pile near $1.5bn. Revenue is tiny. Speculative technology company with a strong retail-investor following but no consumer products.

wiki.title: Quantum computing
wiki.what: Computer hardware technology that uses quantum mechanics
wiki.text: A quantum computer is a computer that represents and processes information using quantum states. Quantum computations exploit phenomena such as superposition, interference, and entanglement. Quantum computers have the potential to complete some calculations exponentially faster than classical computers. For example, a large-scale quantum computer could break widely used encryption schemes and aid physicists in performing physical simulations. However, current hardware implementations of quantum computation are largely experimental and suitable for only certain specialized tasks.

about: Island is a Dallas, Texas-based cybersecurity company, founded in 2020, whose product is the Island Enterprise Browser, a secure workplace browser that gives enterprises control over data and apps for employees and contractors. Customers are large enterprises, with significant adoption among Fortune 500 firms. Backed by Sequoia, Cyberstarts and Insight Partners, it has raised about $1.2 billion at a valuation of over $4 billion. B2B, little brand awareness outside cybersecurity.

Neolix is a Beijing-based autonomous driving company developing self-driving delivery vehicles that carry goods for logistics, retail and city services in China. Founded in 2018, it has deployed large fleets of unmanned vans, and reported raising about $1.3 billion in total, including a 2025 funding round. Customers are e-commerce, express delivery and municipal sanitation operators. B2B, with limited consumer brand awareness.

about: SandboxAQ is a Palo Alto, California company spun out of Alphabet in 2022 by Jack Hidary, building AI and quantum technology products for drug and materials discovery, cybersecurity and navigation (AQNav). It sells software to enterprises and governments in life sciences, chemicals and defence. Raised about $1.5 billion, including from Google, Salesforce, Nvidia and Ray Dalio's fund, at a valuation of $5.75 billion in 2025. B2B deep tech with low consumer brand awareness.

wiki.title: Jack Hidary
wiki.text: Jack D. Hidary is the CEO of AI and quantum technology company SandboxAQ.

about: Sierra is a San Francisco AI startup founded in 2023 by Bret Taylor, former Salesforce co-CEO and OpenAI board chair, and Clay Bavor, that helps businesses build and deploy AI customer-service agents. Customers include large consumer brands and telecoms. Reported funding is about $1.6 billion, with a valuation near $10 billion. B2B software, known in enterprise AI circles with little consumer awareness.

Supabase is a San Francisco-based open-source backend platform for application developers, offering a Postgres database, authentication, storage and real-time APIs, often described as an open-source Firebase alternative. Founded in 2020, it serves developers and startups, with usage-based and subscription revenue. Raised about $1.2 billion in total, including a recent round at a multi-billion valuation. B2B developer tool, strong with developers but little consumer awareness.

Temporal Technologies is a Seattle-based software company, formed in 2019 by the creators of Uber's Cadence, that offers the open-source Temporal platform for durable workflow execution, helping developers build reliable distributed applications and AI agents. Customers include Netflix, Snap and Stripe. Funded by Index, Sequoia, Tiger Global and Andreessen Horowitz, valued around $2.5 billion. B2B developer infrastructure, little consumer awareness.

Advanced Machine Intelligence (AMI Labs) is a Paris-based AI start-up co-founded by Yann LeCun after he left Meta, focused on research into world models and advanced machine intelligence. It reportedly raised close to 890 million euros in early funding. It has no commercial consumer product yet. Research-stage company, known in AI circles through LeCun, with little brand awareness among the public.

B2B finance, known in trading circles, with little consumer brand awareness.

about: OHB System is a Bremen, Germany space systems manufacturer, a subsidiary of OHB SE (Frankfurt: OHB), one of the three large European space companies. It builds satellites and ground systems for Earth observation, navigation (Galileo), telecom and science missions, including SARah and EnMAP, working for ESA, DLR and the German military. Founded in 1958. Customers are space agencies and governments. B2B, little consumer awareness.

Shengshu Technology is a Chinese AI company developing generative AI systems, best known for the Vidu text-to-video model. Founded in 2023 in Beijing and linked to Tsinghua University researchers, it has reported funding of about 6.5 billion yuan. Customers are creators and enterprises using its web service and API. B2B/prosumer, with limited consumer awareness outside China.

about: Socure is a New York-based identity verification and fraud prevention company, founded in 2012, that uses AI and data to verify digital identities, detect fraud and ensure compliance for banks, fintechs, telecoms and government agencies. It acquired Effectiv in 2024 and Qlarifi in 2025. Raised about $900 million, valued at around $4.5 billion. B2B, little consumer awareness.

Xanadu is a Toronto-based quantum computing company, founded in 2016 by Christian Weedbrook, building photonic quantum computers (Aurora) and the PennyLane quantum software library. It serves researchers, enterprises and governments, and announced a plan to list through a SPAC merger with Crane Harbor in 2025. Funding about $986 million reported. B2B deep tech with limited consumer awareness.

Triller is an American social video app, founded in 2015 and merged with TrillerVerz and AGBA in 2024, which lets users create AI-assisted music videos and hosts boxing and other live entertainment events (Triller Fight Club, BKFC). Based in Los Angeles, with a funding total of about $383 million. Listed publicly as Triller Group (Nasdaq: ILLR) after a SPAC with AGBA. Moderate consumer brand awareness, linked to combat sports.

about: Qihoo 360 Technology is a Beijing-based Chinese internet security company founded in 2005 by Zhou Hongyi, offering antivirus software, a browser, search and mobile security, and moving to AI and enterprise security. It was taken private from the NYSE in 2016 and relisted in Shanghai in 2018 (601360). Customers are hundreds of millions of Chinese internet users, with income from advertising and services. Strong brand in China, with very little profile abroad.

Walgreens Boots Alliance (WBA) is a US pharmacy and retail healthcare group headquartered in Deerfield, Illinois, formerly listed on Nasdaq (WBA). Its Walgreens and Boots chains operate about 12,000 stores in the US, UK and Europe, alongside Alliance Healthcare wholesale and the VillageMD care business. Revenue is around 140 billion dollars, mostly pharmacy and retail sales. Founded 1901. Sycamore Partners took it private in a deal completed in 2025. Very high consumer visibility, with sports and community partnerships.

wiki.title: Walgreens Boots Alliance
wiki.text: Walgreens Boots Alliance, Inc. (WBA) was an American multinational holding company headquartered in Deerfield, Illinois. The company was formed on December 31, 2014, after Walgreens bought the 55% stake in Alliance Boots that it did not already own. The total price of the acquisition was $4.9 billion in cash and 144.3 million common shares with fair value of $10.7 billion. Walgreens had previously purchased 45% of the company for $4.0 billion and 83.4 million common shares in August 2012 with an option to purchase the remaining shares within three years.
